newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy awaits EU decision on plan to end milk row.
newsitem.headline: Italy awaits EU decision on plan to end milk row.

text.p: Italy said on Tuesday it was waiting for a decision from Brussels on whether a proposal to end a bitter row over European Union fines for milk overproduction would prove acceptable.

"The government is waiting to hear from Brussels its view on the possibility of making farmers pay a first instalment of the fines immediately, and leaving the rest of the payment until an inquiry commission on quotas has finished work," Prime Minister Romano Prodi's spokesman, Francesco Luna, told reporters.

The government said on Monday after a meeting between Prodi, Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto and farmers' leaders, that it would present a decree law including cheap loans and grants to make up for lost income and a restructuring of milk production.
A government statement on Monday night said those proposals had been given the green light by the European Commission.

Farmers have welcomed the government's plan to set up a commission to examine the whole problem, which centres on EU "super-levy" fines, due to be paid by Friday, for overshooting Italy's 1995-96 milk quota by some 400,000 tonnes.
But they are against paying even a first tranche of the fines because they say the government is to blame for the overproduction problem. The fines add up to some 370 billion lire ($230 million).

Under the present quota system, farmers are allowed to produce 9.9 million tonnes of milk, compared with Italy's total consumption of 18 million tonnes. Pinto has already asked the EU formally to raise Italy's quota to 10.5 million tonnes.

Farmers, who have taken to the streets in their tractors and staged nearly two weeks of protests to press their demands, have largely put their action on ice pending the outcome of talks with the government.
